purpose: How much of a repeating bead cell is actually solid?
meaning: A periodic packing repeats a cell whose boundary spheres are shared with neighboring cells. Simple cubic packing has eight corner eighths, totaling one sphere, and cell edge a=2r. Face-centered cubic packing adds six face halves, totaling four spheres, with face-diagonal contacts giving a=2√2r. Dividing occupied sphere volume by cube volume gives packing fraction η, which is independent of radius within each packing.

definition.setting: A materials model repeats one cube of equal solid beads. Compare corner-only simple cubic packing with face-centered cubic packing, accounting for the bead pieces shared by neighboring cubes.
definition.formal_latex: \eta=\frac{N(4\pi r^3/3)}{a^3},\qquad a=2r\text{ for SC},\quad a=2\sqrt{2}r\text{ for FCC}.

signature.k: Discrete packing choice: 1 simple cubic or 2 face-centered cubic

conditions: Choose integer packing 1 simple cubic or 2 face-centered cubic, and equal sphere radii 0.5–1.5 cm. Use periodic unit-cell sharing and nearest-neighbor contacts. The displayed face-plane circular sections do not measure three-dimensional occupancy by their flat area. No comparison with all possible packings or real materials is asserted.
definition.domain_notes: Choose 1 simple cubic or 2 face-centered cubic, with equal sphere radius 0.5–1.5 centimetres. Boundary spheres are shared periodically: corners contribute eighths and face centers halves. The picture is the plane containing one boundary face, with full circular sections of boundary spheres; it does not measure the three-dimensional occupied fraction by flat area. SC contacts follow cube edges; FCC contacts follow a face diagonal through its face center. A separate fixed 0–1 bar measures the volume fraction. No densest-packing proof or real-material prediction is claimed.

grammar.formation_rule: A periodic packing repeats a cell whose boundary spheres are shared with neighboring cells. Simple cubic packing has eight corner eighths, totaling one sphere, and cell edge a=2r. Face-centered cubic packing adds six face halves, totaling four spheres, with face-diagonal contacts giving a=2√2r. grammar.precedence: Each corner sphere is shared among eight adjacent cells and each face-center sphere among two. Thus equivalent counts are 8/8=1 for SC and 8/8+6/2=4 for FCC. SC neighbors touch along an edge, making a=2r. FCC corner-to-face-center-to-corner contacts span a face diagonal of length 4r, while that diagonal is √2a. Insert the resulting edge length and equivalent sphere count into occupied sphere volume divided by a³. Both volumes scale as r³, so their ratio does not depend on radius.
